title: Four-state bird counts showed small adjusted temperature slopes in 1990-2024
abstract: We tested survey temperature and recorded bird taxa in California, Oregon, New York, and Pennsylvania. We used accepted Breeding Bird Survey runs and 7,068 consecutive-year pairs with the same route and observer. We fit separate first-difference models in western and eastern states for 1990-2006 and 2007-2024. We adjusted for date, time, duration, assistant status, observer experience, wind, sky, and state-year effects. Slopes ranged from 0.06 to 0.35 additional recorded taxa per 5 C higher start temperature. All point estimates were positive. None excluded zero after correction for four tests. All four corrected intervals were within -1 to +1 taxon per 5 C under the model. Three sensitivity checks gave the same broad result. These are conditional weather associations in accepted survey conditions. They cannot separate detection from ecological change. Missing data, roadside sampling, observer changes, and dependence across routes limit inference. We did not test pollution, extreme heat, long-term warming, or species loss. The package includes code, source hashes, filtered records, model designs, uncertainty estimates, and offline reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Adjusted temperature slopes for two regions and two periods. Thick lines show 95% route-cluster intervals. Thin lines show intervals corrected for four primary tests. All corrected intervals include zero.
